title: Locale-aware candidate gating + scalable staged rollout for rerank upgrades
creator: Aisha R. Khan
description: We need a low-risk, cost-conscious path to upgrade cross-encoder rerank models across locales. Current approach performs full cross-encoder scoring for every candidate set which increases latency and GPU consumption at scale. This ticket proposes a locale-aware gating layer that uses cheap embedding prefilters + per-locale thresholds to skip expensive cross-encoder scoring when unlikely to change top-K, plus a staged rollout orchestration (synthetic workload generator, canary cohorts, automated regression checks) to safely onboard new cross-encoder variants.
background: Customers across EN/ES/FR/APAC report occasional latency spikes during peak QPS when rerankers fallback to larger cross-encoders. We saw a 35% GPU spend increase on rerank during last months holiday spike and a P95 latency regression to ~420ms on some routes. Existing offline evals show modest MRR gains for larger cross-encoder variants but with diminishing returns in low-similarity candidate sets. We need finer-grained decision logic to apply cross-encoders only when expected utility exceeds compute cost and integrate this into our rollout tooling.
proposal: 1) Implement a cheap prefilter: cosine similarity of query/embedding centroid + lightweight mono-encoder score. 2) Per-locale calibrated thresholds: tune skip/prefilter thresholds per locale (en, es, fr, ja, ko, zh) using held-out sets to maintain recall/P@1. 3) Token-length and candidate-count heuristics: gate off cross-encoder when candidate set > 200 or avg token length < 16 and prefilt similarity low. 4) Integrate gating config as a first-class route-level setting in the runtime (defaults + per-customer overrides). 5) Expand our staged rollout pipeline: synthetic workload generator that targets edge cases (low-similarity, code-mixed, LTR languages), automated offline regression checks (MRR, P@1, P@5, latency P95), and auto-rollback on detected regressions or cost overruns. 6) Add telemetry: per-route cross-encoder hit-rate, per-locale quality delta and cost per 1k requests.
acceptance_criteria: Prefilter + gating implemented in runtime and enabled behind feature flag
Per-locale thresholds created and stored in config store with a calibration script
Staged rollout pipeline can run a canary cohort (1% traffic) with synthetic workload and validate metrics automatically
No locale should drop P@1 by >0.8% compared to baseline in canary; overall MRR uplift should be >= 0.8% for routes where cross-encoder remains enabled
Average cross-encoder invocation rate reduced by >= 45% for large-candidate routes without measurable quality loss
Latency P95 for rerank end-to-end decreases by >= 20% on gated routes under production-like load
Cost per 1k requests for rerank endpoints reduced or held steady in rollout; visible in costs dashboard
Runbook for rollback and post-mortem template added to the playbook directory
tasks: Design prefilter scoring function and threshold calibration method (owner: Luca)
Implement runtime gating hook and config API (owner: Runtime team)
Build per-locale calibration harness and dataset extraction (owner: Eval team)
Extend staged rollout service to accept rerank gating configs and synthetic workloads (owner: Orchestrator)
Add telemetry keys: rerank.cross_encoder.calls, rerank.prefilter.skipped, rerank.quality.delta (owner: Observability)
Create dashboards and alert rules for cross-encoder hit-rate and per-locale regressions (owner: Console)
Run three-tiered internal canaries: dev-traffic synthetic, prod-1% canary, prod-10% monitored rollout (owner: SRE)
Post-rollout analysis and cost reconciliation with finance (owner: Growth Ops)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Prefilter false negatives reduce recall for low-resource locales. Mitigation: use conservative thresholds for locales with high tokenization variance and require manual sign-off before enabling for those locales.
Risk: Calibration drift over time as query distribution changes. Mitigation: schedule weekly re-calibration job and monitor stability metrics; enable auto-suggested threshold updates in Console.
Risk: Increased operational complexity for per-route configs. Mitigation: provide sane defaults, a templated UI in Console, and telemetry-based guidance messages.
Risk: Quantization differences across model variants affect score distribution. Mitigation: include quantized model variants in the offline calibration pipeline and adjust thresholds per variant.
Risk: Synthetic workloads miss real-world edge cases. Mitigation: seed synthetic generator with samples from real traffic and incident logs; run shadow-mode validations for 48h before canary.
Risk: Cost savings motivate overly aggressive gating that harms UX. Mitigation: enforce hard quality SLO guardrails in rollout pipeline and automatic rollback triggers.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal dev traffic - feature flag on for team routes; run synthetic generator and compare offline metrics (2 days)
Beta: shadow mode on 5% of prod traffic, no user-facing changes; collect telemetry, check thresholds (3 days)
Canary: enable gating for 1% traffic with live canary cohort; automated checks for quality and cost; abort on failure (72 hours)
Ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 24-48h observation windows between steps and manual sign-off for locales with small datasets
Post-rollout: 14-day monitoring window and cost reconciliation; schedule retrospective and update playbook
metrics_and_sla: Quality: MRR change, P@1, P@5 per-locale, tracked daily
Latency: rerank end-to-end P95 and P99 per-route, target P95 <= 300ms for high-tier routes
Cost: GPU compute minutes and cost per 1k requests for rerank endpoints
Operational: cross-encoder hit-rate, false negative rate of prefilter, frequency of auto-rollbacks
